kind: live observation (not a reconstruction check): whether holding the host native Step pause leaves physics pair/body state untouched by the engine, and what the host setters touch while held

capture.mechanism: private bounded snow-host plugin. Data writes only: the broad-phase object at controller+0x28 had its vtable pointer compare-exchanged to a private copy of the 34-slot table (image RVA 0x29ca8a0) with slot +0x60 (S0 inside 18b8fa0) a forwarding detour; the provider+0x68 pair-collider factory (vtable image RVA 0x29ca780) had slot +8 (18de680) forwarded the same way. A read-only sampler thread swept the 11 guard globals: LockCount/RecursionCount/OwningThread of each CRITICAL_SECTION and count/head of the sibling free-list pool at guard-8, continuously while held and in 20 ms bursts every 200 ms otherwise. on_pause/on_resume callbacks snapshotted the world Step job last-run counter and the PhysicsWorldStep job header (state+0x1b0, reached from world+0xff0 -> physics+0x18, checked by back-link, state+0x10, delegate 0x8ab390 and job vtable 0x1e89618).
capture.frozen_window: from on_pause (host verified the hold) until the sampler first saw the Step last-run counter change after the resume clear; every 18b8fa0 entry, factory call and sampler sweep is tagged with the Step last-run value it saw, so activity in a frozen window is one tagged with the value frozen at on_pause
capture.holds: host simulation.pause (lease 8 s) for about 1.2 s, then simulation.resume; early holds just after the drop-in, main holds between 1.5 s forward (optionally steered) key holds while riding
capture.setter_holds: every third main hold: player.set_velocity with the held velocity x1.0 and x0.9, then player.set_position at the current position; marks timestamp each call window; the coordinator reads both player bodies' +0x10 group words (read-only, external) before and after each call
capture.restore: factory then broad-phase vtable pointer compare-exchanged back after re-checking the owner fields; in-flight detours drained

limits: Wine on macOS, one dispatcher capacity (1) and this CPU count; Windows may differ.

The sampler sees a CRITICAL_SECTION as owned only while some sweep overlaps the hold; very short sections can be missed. The pool count/head check is a second, state-based signal for the pool-taking paths but does not cover guard use without a pool change.
The host setters also enter the protected controller synchronization at controller+0x50, which is not one of the 11 pool guards and was not sampled.
Off-graph services (loading thread, idle task workers) were not separately instrumented; their guard use would have appeared as owned observations or pool changes, and none did while held.
Thread labels are per session and relative (start module and RVA); no thread ids, heap addresses or raw bytes are published.
Live behaviour for these sessions only; not a proof for other game states (sport change, save, online, long holds).
